newsitem.title: UK: Sumitomo probes grind on in U.S., Britain.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo probes grind on in U.S., Britain.

text.p: British and U.S. investigators have yet to finger anyone in the Sumitomo copper mystery as former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka goes on trial in Japan next week.
No conspiracies have been made public. No one has been arrested in Britain or the United States.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) launched its investigation last June on the day Sumitomo Corp rocked financial markets with news of losses that have reached $2.6 billion.
Probes by a U.S. Grand Jury and market watchdog soon followed.
The Japanese conglomerate said Hamanaka confessed to hiding a web of unauthorised deals and prosecutors arrested him last October.
In Britain, the world's hub for industrial metals trading, only a handful of raids have been announced but authorities insist investigations are on track.
Last week, the SFO was thrown off course when the agency itself was taken to court over a raid on a firm of accountants in connection with the Sumitomo case.
The High Court, however, ruled that the SFO was not in contempt of court for seizing computers and downloading data from Kay Accountants Ltd in Radlett, north of London.
"Some of our efforts were diverted into the court proceedings...but it (the Sumitomo case) continues for sure now," an SFO spokeswoman said.
